question.problem:
Suppose the following data is sampled from a population. Compute an estimate for the population mean.

$$
-8,\,5,\,-14,\,-20,\,16
$$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a sequence of random variables representing a random sample of size $n$ drawn from a population with the population mean $\mu .$ 
Then, the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is given by

$$
\overset{―}{X}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{X}_{i}.
$$

Note that:

- $\overset{―}{X}$ is the mean value of ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n},$ while $\overset{¯}{x}$ is the mean of a specific sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$

- the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is an estimator of the population mean $\mu ,$ and

- the value $\overset{^}{\mu }=\overset{¯}{x}$ is an estimate of the population mean $\mu .$

Therefore, our estimate for the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\mu } & =\overset{―}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{5}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(-8+5-14-20+16) \\  & =-\frac{21}{5} \\  & =-4.2.\end{aligned}
$$
